subject: Physics
title: Atoms
summary: Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment showed that all the positive charge and almost all the mass of an atom are in a tiny nucleus (~10⁻¹⁵ m); the rest of the atom is mostly empty.
Problem with Rutherford's model: an orbiting electron should radiate and spiral into the nucleus, and the spectrum should be continuous. In reality atoms are stable and give line spectra.
Bohr proposed that electrons move only in certain orbits where L = nh/2π and do not radiate there. A photon is emitted or absorbed only when the electron jumps between orbits: hν = E_upper − E_lower.
For hydrogen-like atoms (H, He⁺, Li²⁺): r ∝ n²/Z, v ∝ Z/n, E ∝ −Z²/n². The whole hydrogen spectrum (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen…) follows from these.

formulas.name: Distance of closest approach
formulas.formula: r₀ = k (2e)(Ze) / K   (alpha KE = K, head-on)
formulas.when: How close an alpha particle gets — an upper limit on nuclear size.
formulas.mistake: The alpha's charge is 2e, not e.

formulas.name: Impact parameter
formulas.formula: b = k Z e² cot(θ/2) / K   (alpha, KE = K);   b = 0 ⇒ θ = 180° (straight back)
formulas.when: Relation between scattering angle and impact parameter.

formulas.name: Rutherford scattering
formulas.when: How many alphas scatter at a given angle.
formulas.note: Very few particles scatter through large angles.

formulas.name: Radius of nth orbit
formulas.note: r ∝ n²: 4 times at n = 2, 9 times at n = 3.

formulas.name: Energy of nth orbit
formulas.note: Negative means bound. At n = ∞, E = 0.

formulas.name: Time period, frequency, current
formulas.formula: T ∝ n³/Z²,   f ∝ Z²/n³,   current I = ef ∝ Z²/n³

formulas.name: Photon in a transition
formulas.formula: hν = E_{n₂} − E_{n₁};   1/λ = R Z² (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²),   R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹
formulas.note: Always n₂ > n₁; the R formula works only for hydrogen-like atoms.

formulas.name: Spectral series of hydrogen
formulas.formula: Lyman n₁ = 1 (UV) · Balmer n₁ = 2 (visible) · Paschen n₁ = 3 (IR) · Brackett 4 (IR) · Pfund 5 (IR)
formulas.when: Which series a line belongs to.

formulas.name: Series limits
formulas.formula: Shortest λ (series limit): n₂ = ∞ ⇒ 1/λ = RZ²/n₁².  Longest λ: n₂ = n₁ + 1
formulas.when: Shortest and longest wavelength in a series.

formulas.name: Number of spectral lines
formulas.formula: total lines when falling from level n = n(n − 1)/2
formulas.note: A single atom can give at most (n − 1) lines at a time.

formulas.name: Ionisation and excitation energy
formulas.formula: Ionisation (from ground): 13.6 Z² eV.  H first excitation (1 → 2): 10.2 eV,  1 → 3: 12.09 eV
formulas.note: Ionisation potential is in volt (13.6 V), energy in eV.

formulas.name: de Broglie view of Bohr orbit
formulas.when: Wave meaning of Bohr's condition: a whole number of waves fits in the orbit.

examples.title: How close does the alpha get?
examples.problem: A 7.7 MeV alpha particle heads straight at a gold nucleus (Z = 79). Distance of closest approach?
examples.solution: r₀ = k(2e)(79e)/K with K = 7.7 × 10⁶ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. r₀ = 9 × 10⁹ × 158 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ / 7.7 × 10⁶ ≈ 3.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ m (≈ 30 fm). The nucleus is smaller still.

topics.title: Alpha-particle scattering (Geiger–Marsden)
topics.explain: Alpha particles were fired at a thin gold foil. Most passed straight through (the atom is mostly empty); some were deflected through large angles; very few (about 1 in 8000) were deflected by more than 90°, a few even bounced straight back — showing a small, heavy, positive nucleus. Gold was used because it can be beaten into very thin foil.

topics.title: Rutherford model and its drawbacks
topics.explain: Nucleus at the centre with electrons revolving around it (planetary model). Drawbacks: an accelerating charge radiates, so the electron should spiral in (atom unstable), and the spectrum should be continuous — neither happens.

topics.title: Bohr's three postulates
topics.explain: (1) Electrons revolve in certain stationary orbits without radiating. (2) These are the orbits with L = nh/2π. (3) On changing orbit, a photon with hν = E_i − E_f is emitted or absorbed. Bohr's model works only for one-electron atoms (H, He⁺, Li²⁺).

topics.title: Energy level diagram
topics.explain: Levels get closer together going up (E ∝ −1/n²). Ground state n = 1 (−13.6 eV), first excited n = 2 (−3.4 eV), n = 3 (−1.51 eV), … n = ∞ (0 eV).

topics.title: Hydrogen spectrum
topics.explain: Emission spectrum: bright lines when electrons fall to lower levels; absorption spectrum: dark lines when they jump up. Lyman is in the UV, Balmer in the visible (Hα red, 656 nm), Paschen and beyond in the IR.

topics.title: Limitations of Bohr's model
topics.explain: It cannot explain spectra of multi-electron atoms, the relative intensities of lines, or fine structure. It is a semi-classical model.

topics.title: Scaling with Z and n
topics.explain: r ∝ n²/Z, v ∝ Z/n, E ∝ Z²/n², T ∝ n³/Z², f ∝ Z²/n³. Ratio questions are solved in one line with these.

ratta: Eₙ = −13.6 Z²/n² eV;  rₙ = 0.529 n²/Z Å;  vₙ = 2.18 × 10⁶ Z/n m/s.
R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹;  Lyman limit 91.2 nm;  Hα 656 nm.
Series: Lyman 1 (UV), Balmer 2 (visible), Paschen 3, Brackett 4, Pfund 5 (IR).
H: ionisation 13.6 eV, first excitation 10.2 eV.  He⁺: 54.4 eV.
